status: drafted via lean single-pass workflow grounded in the real extracted verse text
notes: Extremely short single-chapter text (27 verses) — the mid-fragment of the larger "Song of the Three Holy Children" insertion into Daniel 3, extracted here as its own standalone book per this translation's file layout. Structure: vv.1-22 are Azarias's prayer of confession/covenant-appeal spoken while walking in the fire; vv.23-25 narrate the king's servants stoking the furnace and Chaldeans being burned by the overflow; vv.26-27 narrate the angel of the Lord's deliverance. Two person tiers cover the whole book cleanly — there is no law/ritual teaching content of the kind that would warrant a role:"law" tier (the prayer itself is confession/petition, not instruction). NAMING-COLLISION / IDENTIFICATION NOTE (rule 8 applied): Azarias is traditionally understood as the Hebrew name of Abednego, one of Daniel's three companions in Daniel 3 — but THIS text never says so; it never mentions Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach, or Abednego by name, and never states Azarias is the same figure. Per the explicit rule against asserting a link the text itself doesn't make, genealogy/identity here is drawn ONLY from what's on the page: an unnamed man named Azarias, praying in an unnamed furnace, with unnamed "fellows." No father/mother/spouse/children are stated. "Fellows" (v.1, v.26) are never individually named in this excerpt, so per the undifferentiated-group rule they are one collective submanager, not invented individuals. The king's servants and the Chaldeans burned by the flame (vv.23-25) are likewise undifferentiated groups, logged only in genealogyLists, not promoted to characters. Abraham, Isaac, and "Israel" (Jacob) are invoked by name in the prayer's covenant appeal (v.12-13) but are not acting characters in this scene — already indexed elsewhere as Genesis figures — so logged as a bulk reference only, not re-indexed.

characters.name: Azarias

verses.note: Azarias stands up in the midst of the fire and opens his mouth to pray.
Blesses God's name and declares all His judgments true and righteous.
Confesses that Jerusalem's fall and the people's disgrace came justly, because of real sin and disobedience.
Pleads that God not abandon them or break the covenant, appealing to His promises to Abraham, Isaac, and Israel.
Laments that the nation now has no prince, prophet, leader, or place to sacrifice.
Offers a contrite heart and humble spirit in place of burnt offerings, vowing to follow God wholly.
Asks God to act for His own name's sake, put their enemies to shame, and prove Himself the only God before the whole world.

funFacts: Prays this entire supplication while physically standing inside the burning furnace, per v.2.

verses.note: Walk in the midst of the fire together, praising and blessing God alongside Azarias.
Present with Azarias when the angel of the Lord comes down into the oven.

characters.name: The Angel of the Lord

verses.note: Comes down into the oven together with Azarias and his fellows and smites out the flame of the fire.
Turns the furnace's midst into a moist, whistling wind so the fire does not touch, hurt, or trouble them at all.

funFacts: The furnace flame is said to have streamed 49 cubits above the furnace (v.24) before the angel's intervention brought total protection.

genealogyLists.note: Bulk/unresolved references kept out of the character list.

kings_servants.note: Unnamed servants of the king who keep the furnace stoked hot with rosin, pitch, tow, and small wood.

chaldeans_burned.note: Unnamed Chaldeans standing about the furnace, burned by the flame that streamed out through it.

abraham_isaac_israel_covenant.note: Invoked by name in Azarias's covenant appeal as the fathers to whom God promised to multiply their seed like the stars of heaven; already indexed as their own characters in the Genesis roster, not re-indexed here.
